citation.title: Acute effects of elbow flexion and knee extension exercises on vascular and hemodynamic parameters and arterial stiffness indices in healthy young adults
citation.journal: BMC Sports Science, Medicine and Rehabilitation

reported.what: peripheral systolic blood pressure at baseline, T0 (immediately after) and T15 for elbow flexion and knee extension at 50% of 1RM, mean ± SD, n = 35 young men (Table 1); the bout is set by percent of a one-repetition maximum in kg, with no oxygen uptake or watts printed

location.where: Table 1, row pSBP, columns EFlex and KExt

reported.what: heart rate at baseline, T0 and T15 for the same two bouts, mean ± SD (Table 2); baseline is a seated value taken before the exercise with no stated rest or run-in duration, and no fasting or meal is described (morning visit, no caffeine, excess fat or alcohol)

location.where: Table 2, row Heart rate, columns EFlex and KExt

detail: The only intervention is a resistance bout at 50% of 1RM (3 sets to fatigue), whose oxygen uptake or watts the paper never prints, so no activity level can be given; the pre-exercise baselines have no printed run-in and no stated fast or meal (a morning visit with only caffeine, fat and alcohol avoided), and the model markers are limited to heart rate and blood pressure.
